knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Ueshima_2025_remimazolam"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Ueshima_2025_remimazolam"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-10015-z> (open access)

Ueshima et al. sampled remimazolam, its inactive carboxylic-acid metabolite
CNS 7054, and the bispectral index (BIS) during the first minutes of a
remimazolam-only induction of general anesthesia, before any opioid was given.
Remimazolam follows a three-compartment model; all of its clearance passes
through one transit compartment into a two-compartment CNS 7054 model. The BIS
falls from a fixed baseline of 100 through a maximum-inhibition (Emax) model
driven by an effect compartment. Only body weight was retained as a covariate,
on remimazolam clearance. Because each patient contributed only three samples,
the peripheral and transit parameters (V3, Q2, Q3, kT, V2M, Q2M) and the
effect-site rate constant kE0 were fixed at published values from healthy
volunteers (Schuttler 2020; Zhou 2020).

# Population

Twenty Japanese adults (12 male, 8 female) underwent general anesthesia at
Yamagata University Hospital between April 2021 and October 2022 (Ueshima 2025
Table 1). The median age was 71.7 years (range 42.2-88.6), and 14 of 20
patients (70%) were 65 or older. The median body weight was 60.4 kg (44.5-77.1)
and the median BMI 23.1 kg/m^2 (18.1-28.0). Renal and hepatic markers were
mostly normal: serum creatinine 0.81 mg/dL (0.50-1.28), Cockcroft-Gault
creatinine clearance 72.6 mL/min (41.6-115.6), AST 21 IU/L and ALT 21 IU/L.
Patients with Child-Pugh C cirrhosis were excluded. Remimazolam was infused at
12 mg/kg/h until loss of consciousness (median 1.71 min, range 1.20-3.00) and
then at 1 mg/kg/h. Plasma and BIS were sampled 1, 3 and 5 min after loss of
consciousness, giving 60 records of each.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Ueshima_2025_remimazolam")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Ueshima_2025_remimazolam.R`. The table below
collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL at 60.4 kg) | log(1.38) L/min | Table 2 |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.75, fixed | Table 2 row equation; Methods Eq. 3 ("set to 0.75" for clearance) |
| `lvc` (V1) | log(6.38) L | Table 2 |
| `lvp` (V2) | log(4.11) L | Table 2 |
| `lvp2` (V3) | log(15.5) L, fixed | Table 2 (literature value, Schuttler 2020) |
| `lq` (Q2) | log(1.04) L/min, fixed | Table 2 (literature value) |
| `lq2` (Q3) | log(0.19) L/min, fixed | Table 2 (literature value) |
| `lktr` (kT) | log(0.024) 1/min, fixed | Table 3 (literature value); Methods |
| `lcl_cns7054` (CLM) | log(0.123) L/min | Table 3 |
| `lvc_cns7054` (V1M) | log(0.423) L | Table 3 |
| `lvp_cns7054` (V2M) | log(7.4) L per 75 kg, fixed | Table 3 row equation V2M = theta x (BW/75) |
| `lq_cns7054` (Q2M) | log(0.13) L/min per 75 kg, fixed | Table 3 row equation Q2M = theta x (BW/75) |
| `lec50` (EC50) | log(79.6) ng/mL | Table 4 |
| `limax` (Emax) | log(54.0) | Table 4 |
| `lke0` (kE0) | log(0.135) 1/min, fixed | Table 4 (literature value, Zhou 2020) |
| `etalcl` | 16.3% -> 0.0262 | Table 2 |
| `etalvc` | 89.9% -> 0.5923 | Table 2 |
| `etalcl_cns7054` | 66.7% -> 0.3680 | Table 3 |
| `etalvc_cns7054` | 57.6% -> 0.2865 | Table 3 |
| `etalec50` | 98.6% -> 0.6791 | Table 4 |
| `expSd`, `expSd_cns7054`, `expSd_BIS` | 0.0879, 0.0918, 0.138 | Tables 2, 3, 4; exponential error, Methods Eq. 1 |
| Structure: 3-cmt remimazolam -> transit -> 2-cmt CNS 7054; effect compartment | n/a | Figure 1; Methods; Supplementary Table 1 (model 1 selected) |
| `BIS = 100 - Emax * Ce / (EC50 + Ce)` | n/a | Methods Eq. 5 |
| `P_i = theta * exp(eta_i)` | n/a | Methods Eq. 2 |

# Virtual cohorts

Two virtual cohorts are simulated.

* **Figure 4 cohorts.** The paper's Figure 4 simulates patients weighing 40, 60
  and 80 kg given 12 mg/kg/h until loss of consciousness at 1.71 min and then
  1 mg/kg/h. One arm of 200 virtual patients per weight is built here on a
  dense 0-10 min grid.
* **Study cohort.** To compare against the observed medians in Table 1, 200
  virtual patients have weights drawn around the cohort median (60.4 kg,
  truncated to the observed 44.5-77.1 kg) and loss-of-consciousness times
  drawn around the observed median (1.71 min, truncated to 1.20-3.00 min).
  Each is sampled 1, 3 and 5 min after loss of consciousness, as in the study.

The model declares three endpoints (`Cc`, `Cc_cns7054`, `BIS`), so every
observation row carries `dvid = 1L` alongside the named dosing compartment
`cmt = "central"`; rxode2 still returns all three endpoints at every row.

```{r cohort}
# rxode2's simulation streams are partitioned per solver thread, so the
# cohorts below differ between machines with different thread counts. Every
# assertion downstream is written to hold for any cohort the model produces.
set.seed(20251)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20251)

induction_rate <- 12 / 60 # mg/kg/min (12 mg/kg/h)
maintenance_rate <- 1 / 60 # mg/kg/min (1 mg/kg/h)

# One subject's events: induction infusion until loss of consciousness
# (tloc), then maintenance until tend; observations at obs_times.
subject_events <- function(id, WT, tloc, tend, obs_times) {
  doses <- tibble(
    id = id,
    time = c(0, tloc),
    rate = c(induction_rate, maintenance_rate) * WT,
    amt = c(induction_rate * WT * tloc, maintenance_rate * WT * (tend - tloc)),
    evid = 1L,
    cmt = "central",
    dvid = NA_integer_
  )
  obs <- tibble(
    id = id,
    time = obs_times,
    rate = NA_real_,
    amt = NA_real_,
    evid = 0L,
    cmt = "central",
    dvid = 1L
  )
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |> mutate(WT = WT, tloc = tloc)
}

# Figure 4 cohorts: 200 per weight, loss of consciousness at 1.71 min.
n_per_arm <- 200
fig4_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 10, by = 0.05), 1.71)))
fig4_wts <- c(40, 60, 80)
events_fig4 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(fig4_wts), function(k) {
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_per_arm), function(i) {
    subject_events(
      id = (k - 1L) * n_per_arm + i,
      WT = fig4_wts[k],
      tloc = 1.71,
      tend = 10,
      obs_times = fig4_grid
    )
  })) |>
    mutate(arm = paste0(fig4_wts[k], " kg"))
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_fig4[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

# Study cohort: weight and time to loss of consciousness drawn around the
# Table 1 medians and truncated to the observed ranges.
n_study <- 200
study_wt <- pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_study, 60.4, 8), 44.5), 77.1)
study_tloc <- pmin(pmax(1.71 * exp(rnorm(n_study, 0, 0.25)), 1.20), 3.00)
events_study <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_study), function(i) {
  subject_events(
    id = 1000L + i,
    WT = study_wt[i],
    tloc = study_tloc[i],
    tend = study_tloc[i] + 5,
    obs_times = study_tloc[i] + c(1, 3, 5)
  )
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_study[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Ueshima_2025_remimazolam")

sim_fig4 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events_fig4,
  keep = c("WT", "arm"),
  useLinCmt = FALSE
) |>
  as.data.frame()

sim_study <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events_study,
  keep = c("WT", "tloc"),
  useLinCmt = FALSE
) |>
  as.data.frame()

# Typical-value (no IIV, no residual error) profiles for the Figure 4 weights.
mod_typical <- mod |> rxode2::zeroRe()
events_typ <- events_fig4 |> filter(id %in% (c(0L, 1L, 2L) * n_per_arm + 1L))
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typical,
  events = events_typ,
  keep = c("WT", "arm"),
  useLinCmt = FALSE
) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# Replicate Figure 4

Figure 4 of Ueshima 2025 plots the median of 1000 simulated profiles for each
weight: (a) plasma remimazolam, (b) effect-site remimazolam, and (c) BIS. The
plots below show the median and the 5th-95th percentile band of the simulated
individual predictions (`Cc`, `effect` and the noise-free BIS are the model's
predictions; the residual error is not added).

```{r figure-4, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 3.5}
fig4_long <- sim_fig4 |>
  select(id, time, arm, Cc, effect, BIS) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, effect, BIS), names_to = "quantity", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(
    quantity = factor(
      quantity,
      levels = c("Cc", "effect", "BIS"),
      labels = c("(a) Plasma RMZ (ng/mL)", "(b) Effect-site RMZ (ng/mL)", "(c) BIS")
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(arm, quantity, time) |>
  summarise(
    q05 = quantile(value, 0.05),
    q50 = median(value),
    q95 = quantile(value, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(fig4_long, aes(time, q50, colour = arm, fill = arm)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.12, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~quantity, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after starting infusion (min)",
    y = NULL,
    colour = "Body weight",
    fill = "Body weight",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Ueshima 2025 (lines: medians; bands: 5th-95th percentiles)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The paper's Figure 4 medians were digitised by the maintainers. The table
compares them with the median of the simulated cohort at the same weight and
with the model's typical-value (no IIV) profile.

```{r figure-4-compare}
fig4_digitised <- tribble(
  ~arm, ~quantity, ~time, ~published,
  "40 kg", "Cc", 1.71, 1652,
  "60 kg", "Cc", 1.71, 2359,
  "80 kg", "Cc", 1.71, 3054,
  "40 kg", "Cc", 3, 1174,
  "60 kg", "Cc", 3, 1522,
  "80 kg", "Cc", 3, 1815,
  "40 kg", "Cc", 5, 859,
  "60 kg", "Cc", 5, 1054,
  "80 kg", "Cc", 5, 1196,
  "40 kg", "Cc", 10, 685,
  "60 kg", "Cc", 10, 804,
  "80 kg", "Cc", 10, 902,
  "40 kg", "effect", 3, 392,
  "60 kg", "effect", 3, 559,
  "80 kg", "effect", 3, 703,
  "40 kg", "effect", 8, 635,
  "60 kg", "effect", 8, 817,
  "80 kg", "effect", 8, 954,
  "60 kg", "BIS", 10, 52
)

as_long <- function(d) {
  d |>
    select(id, arm, time, Cc, effect, BIS) |>
    pivot_longer(c(Cc, effect, BIS), names_to = "quantity", values_to = "value")
}
sim_median <- as_long(sim_fig4) |>
  group_by(arm, quantity, time) |>
  summarise(sim_median = median(value), .groups = "drop")
typ_value <- as_long(sim_typ) |>
  select(arm, quantity, time, typical = value)

fig4_check <- fig4_digitised |>
  left_join(sim_median, by = c("arm", "quantity", "time")) |>
  left_join(typ_value, by = c("arm", "quantity", "time")) |>
  mutate(
    pct_median = 100 * (sim_median - published) / published,
    pct_typical = 100 * (typical - published) / published
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(fig4_check) == nrow(fig4_digitised),
  !anyNA(fig4_check$sim_median),
  !anyNA(fig4_check$typical)
)

fig4_check |>
  mutate(
    across(c(sim_median, typical), \(x) signif(x, 4)),
    across(c(pct_median, pct_typical), \(x) round(x, 1))
  ) |>
  rename(
    "Weight" = arm,
    "Quantity" = quantity,
    "Time (min)" = time,
    "Figure 4 median (digitised)" = published,
    "Simulated median" = sim_median,
    "Difference, median (%)" = pct_median,
    "Typical value" = typical,
    "Difference, typical (%)" = pct_typical
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated medians and typical values vs. digitised Figure 4 medians.")

# The typical-value peak is deterministic, so that check is tight: a misread
# clearance, volume, weight exponent or dose unit moves it by tens of
# percent. The simulated medians come from 200 patients per arm, whose median
# carries a Monte Carlo error of several percent at the peak (IIV on V1 is
# 89.9%), so they are gated on their average and with a per-point envelope.
peak <- fig4_check$quantity == "Cc" & fig4_check$time == 1.71
stopifnot(
  all(abs(fig4_check$pct_typical[peak]) < 5),
  mean(abs(fig4_check$pct_median)) < 8,
  all(abs(fig4_check$pct_median) < 20)
)
```

The simulated medians follow the digitised curves within a few percent at
every time and weight. The typical-value curve matches the peak but runs up
to 13% above the median plasma concentration during redistribution
(3-5 min). With the large IIV on V1, the median of the stochastic profiles
falls below the typical-value curve once redistribution dominates, which is
why Figure 4 is compared with the simulated median rather than the typical
value.

# Observed medians (Table 1)

Table 1 reports the median and range of all 60 observed remimazolam and
CNS 7054 concentrations and BIS values, pooled over the 1, 3 and 5 min
samples. The study cohort is compared with these after adding residual error
(`sim`, the simulated observation).

```{r table-1}
# rxode2 returns the simulated observation (with residual error) for the
# endpoint whose dvid is on the row in `sim`; derive the other two from
# their individual predictions with the model's own log-normal error.
sd_tab <- c(
  Cc = 0.0879,
  Cc_cns7054 = 0.0918,
  BIS = 0.138
)
study_obs <- sim_study |>
  mutate(
    obs_Cc = Cc * exp(rnorm(n(), 0, sd_tab[["Cc"]])),
    obs_cns7054 = Cc_cns7054 * exp(rnorm(n(), 0, sd_tab[["Cc_cns7054"]])),
    obs_BIS = BIS * exp(rnorm(n(), 0, sd_tab[["BIS"]]))
  )

table1 <- tibble(
  quantity = c("Remimazolam (ng/mL)", "CNS 7054 (ng/mL)", "BIS"),
  published_median = c(1159, 485, 53),
  published_range = c("745.4-2471.3", "103-1568.9", "36-83"),
  sim_median = c(
    median(study_obs$obs_Cc),
    median(study_obs$obs_cns7054),
    median(study_obs$obs_BIS)
  ),
  sim_p05 = c(
    quantile(study_obs$obs_Cc, 0.05),
    quantile(study_obs$obs_cns7054, 0.05),
    quantile(study_obs$obs_BIS, 0.05)
  ),
  sim_p95 = c(
    quantile(study_obs$obs_Cc, 0.95),
    quantile(study_obs$obs_cns7054, 0.95),
    quantile(study_obs$obs_BIS, 0.95)
  )
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim_median - published_median) / published_median)

table1 |>
  mutate(across(c(sim_median, sim_p05, sim_p95), \(x) signif(x, 3)), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  rename(
    "Quantity" = quantity,
    "Table 1 median" = published_median,
    "Table 1 range" = published_range,
    "Simulated median" = sim_median,
    "Simulated 5th pct" = sim_p05,
    "Simulated 95th pct" = sim_p95,
    "Median difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Pooled 1/3/5-min observations: simulated study cohort vs. Ueshima 2025 Table 1.")

# Medians over 600 pooled samples. A mis-scaled dose, volume or EC50 moves
# these by far more than the bounds; the bounds leave room for the
# approximated weight and loss-of-consciousness distributions.
stopifnot(abs(table1$pct_diff) < c(20, 35, 10))
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA table. PKNCA is run on the simulated Figure 4
cohorts over the 0-10 min window to obtain Cmax, Tmax and AUC0-10 of
remimazolam and CNS 7054 per weight. Remimazolam Cmax and Tmax are then
compared with the digitised peak of Figure 4a.

```{r pknca}
dose_df <- events_fig4 |>
  filter(evid == 1L) |>
  select(id, time, amt, arm)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id)

intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 10, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)

nca_parent_in <- sim_fig4 |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, arm)
nca_parent <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_parent_in, Cc ~ time | arm + id),
  dose_obj,
  intervals = intervals
))

nca_metab_in <- sim_fig4 |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc_cns7054)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc_cns7054, arm)
nca_metab <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_metab_in, Cc_cns7054 ~ time | arm + id),
  dose_obj,
  intervals = intervals
))

summary(nca_parent)
summary(nca_metab)
```

```{r nca-compare}
published_nca <- tribble(
  ~arm, ~cmax, ~tmax,
  "40 kg", 1652, 1.71,
  "60 kg", 2359, 1.71,
  "80 kg", 3054, 1.71
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_parent,
  reference = published_nca,
  by = "arm",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "min"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)

knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Remimazolam NCA (median of 200 simulated patients per weight) vs. the digitised Figure 4a peak. * differs by >20%."
)
```

No row differs by more than 20%. The simulated Tmax is the end of the
induction infusion, as in Figure 4a.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **IIV percentages read as CVs.** Tables 2-4 give the inter-individual
  variability as a percentage for the exponential model of Methods Eq. 2,
  without stating whether it is a CV or the square root of the variance x
  100. The percentages were converted with `omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1)`. The
  confidence intervals are symmetric on the percentage scale and so cannot
  separate the two readings. The reading matters for the wide rows: under
  the square-root reading the variances of V1, CLM, V1M and EC50 would be
  0.808, 0.445, 0.332 and 0.972 instead of 0.592, 0.368, 0.287 and 0.679.
  Figure 4 does not settle it either: with 1000 simulated patients per
  weight, both readings reproduce the digitised plasma and effect-site
  medians within about 2-3% on average (the CV reading fits the effect-site
  curve slightly better, 1.2% vs 3.4% mean absolute difference), which is
  within the Monte Carlo and digitising error.
- **EC50 IIV taken from Table 4 (98.6%), not the Results text (35.1%).** The
  Results paragraph says "The inter-individual variability for EC50 was
  35.1%", while Table 4 prints 98.6% with a 95% CI of 29.8-167%, an RSE of
  35.6% and a bootstrap median of 98.0%. The table value is internally
  consistent (98.6 +/- 1.96 x 0.356 x 98.6 reproduces the printed interval),
  the bootstrap agrees, and every other variability in the Results text
  matches its table, so the text value was treated as a typographical error.
- **Weight on CNS 7054 V2M and Q2M is linear per 75 kg.** Methods say that
  body weight was included allometrically on all disposition parameters with
  exponents 0.75 for clearance and 1 for volume. The final-model row
  equations in Tables 2 and 3, however, apply weight only to CL
  (`(BW/60.4)^0.75`) and to the literature-fixed V2M and Q2M as `(BW/75)`
  with units of "L/75 kg" and "L/min/75 kg". The printed equations were
  followed, so Q2M scales with exponent 1 and V1, V2, V3, Q2, Q3, CLM and V1M
  are not weight-scaled.
- **Doses are remimazolam base.** Anerem is labelled and dosed as remimazolam,
  and the simulated peak at loss of consciousness reproduces Figure 4a within
  2% without a salt correction (a besylate-to-base factor would lower it by
  about 26%).
- **No molecular-weight conversion between parent and metabolite.** The
  paper does not state one, so remimazolam clearance enters the transit
  compartment 1:1 by mass, and the CNS 7054 volumes and clearance are
  apparent values on that basis.
- **Fixed literature values.** kT, V3, V2M, Q2, Q3 and Q2M are the values
  printed in Tables 2 and 3 (from Schuttler 2020), and kE0 = 0.135 1/min is
  the value printed in Table 4 (from Zhou 2020). They were not re-derived
  from those papers.
- **Residual error.** The exponential residual error of Methods Eq. 1
  (`C = C_pred x exp(epsilon)`) is encoded as `lnorm()` with the tabulated
  percentage as the log-scale SD, for remimazolam, CNS 7054 and BIS.
- **Sequential fit encoded jointly.** The authors fitted the PD on each
  patient's Bayesian PK estimates. The packaged model links the PK and PD
  directly, which is equivalent for simulation.
- **Virtual-cohort covariates.** The individual weights and
  loss-of-consciousness times are not published. The study cohort draws
  weight from a normal distribution (mean 60.4 kg, SD 8 kg) and the
  loss-of-consciousness time from a log-normal distribution (median
  1.71 min, log-SD 0.25), each truncated to the Table 1 range.
- **Errata.** Crossref registered no correction or update for the article
  as of 2026-11-05.
